chapter: Ellington band: drinking, quarrels and rent parties
title: Sonny Greer's drinking and the Kansas City druggist's fake drink
summary: Duke had a Kansas City druggist serve Sonny a fake drink, which made Sonny pass out anyway; Bigard adds that Sonny had a phenomenal memory for names.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You're talking about in Kansas City?

Yeah, we were in Kansas City and Sonny used to get stoned every night so much and Duke was getting after him. Duke was getting after him to stop drinking so much because it was interfering with his music.

So they had a drug store in Kansas City that this druggist was taking alcohol and doctoring it up with the flavor of lemon or anything like that and the guys used to go in there and buy it as a drink. Now, Sonny's cold sober, so he found out where this druggist and who he was and he goes in there to get him a drink, and Duke had told the druggist, "Don't give him a drink. Just give him fake anything."

So sure enough Sonny walks in there and said, "Hi, Bud. Hi, pal. You know, fix me up one there." The druggist said, "Okay." So he fixed him up a glass and it looked like gin and put a little lemon flavor on it. And Sonny said, "How much?" He said, "$2," because it was a big drink. And Sonny, you know, he drank that and he got off the stool and fell down. He was drunk.

Now, that's how much he used to drink. And it's just terrible because he's such a likable guy. You know, like, if somebody walks in the place and go to Duke and, you know, talk to him and have a conversation, and Duke would

kind of remember his face but he couldn't remember his name. And when the person would leave he'd ask Sonny, "Sonny, who was that?" Right off the bat, Sonny said, "Don't you know him? That's so and so and so and so."
Whether he was sober or not?
Yeah, sober or not. He's got a phenomenal memory about people.
